items.meaning: something that has both advantages and disadvantages
items.example: Social media is a double-edged sword: it connects people but can also spread misinformation.

items.meaning: a small, visible part of a much larger problem
items.example: The reported cases of plastic pollution are only the tip of the iceberg.

items.meaning: an amount too small to make a real difference
items.example: Planting a few trees in the city centre is a drop in the ocean compared with what is needed.

items.meaning: very different from something
items.example: Today’s smartphones are a far cry from the bulky mobile phones of the 1990s.

items.meaning: an idea that makes you think seriously
items.example: The documentary about fast fashion gave me a lot of food for thought.

items.meaning: something very easy to do
items.example: The first part of the test was a piece of cake, but the essay was harder.
items.care: Informal — fine in Speaking, avoid in Academic Writing.

items.meaning: to study hard
items.example: I've got to hit the books this weekend because my exam is on Monday.

items.meaning: very rarely
items.example: I eat fast food once in a blue moon, usually when I'm travelling.

items.meaning: slightly ill
items.example: I felt a bit under the weather last week, so I stayed at home.

items.meaning: to work or study late into the night
items.example: Before deadlines, many students burn the midnight oil to finish their projects.
items.care: Informal — natural in Speaking; use a neutral phrase in essays.

items.meaning: over a long period of time; eventually
items.example: Investing in public transport will save money in the long run.

items.meaning: a situation where one problem causes another that makes the first worse
items.example: Poverty and poor education can form a vicious circle that is hard to break.

items.meaning: to watch or monitor something carefully
items.example: Parents should keep an eye on how much time children spend online.

items.meaning: to make more effort than is expected
items.example: The best employees are often those who go the extra mile for customers.
items.care: Slightly informal — better in Speaking than in essays.

items.meaning: the most important fact or consideration
items.example: The bottom line is that companies will not change unless it is profitable.
items.care: Informal as a sentence opener — avoid in Academic Writing.

items.meaning: modern, or having the latest information
items.example: It is hard for schools to keep their equipment up to date.

items.meaning: a situation where you must learn a lot very quickly
items.example: Starting my first job was a steep learning curve, especially with new software.

items.meaning: to make people feel more relaxed when they first meet
items.example: Our teacher used a quick game to break the ice on the first day.

items.meaning: to agree with someone
items.example: My parents and I don't always see eye to eye about my career plans.

items.meaning: something that has good and bad effects
items.example: Tourism is a mixed blessing for small islands: it brings jobs but damages nature.

items.meaning: in a quiet place that few people visit
items.example: I prefer holidays off the beaten track, away from crowded resorts.

items.meaning: to have just enough money to pay for basic needs
items.example: Rising rents mean many young workers struggle to make ends meet.

items.meaning: at a point where an important decision must be made
items.example: Many countries are at a crossroads between fossil fuels and clean energy.

items.meaning: to fail to appreciate something because it is always there
items.example: In wealthy countries, people often take clean water for granted.

items.meaning: to learn how to do a job or activity
items.example: It took me a few weeks to learn the ropes at my part-time job.
